classification: Overlap and continuation audit, not a new arithmetic result

findings.claim: A positive coefficient cone can miss the target
findings.comparison: Existing mechanism, different cones. NS62/64 concern nonnegative adjacent-difference coefficients; NS96 LCM-grouped coefficients can have either sign. Neither cone is identified with the other.
findings.disposition: Do not report a new general positivity wall.

findings.claim: The complete c=+q LCM rule fails to converge
findings.comparison: NS78 already forces c1 to -1 under norm convergence; this rule has c1=Gamma11>=0. The qualitative failure is an immediate consequence. NS96 adds an explicit local constant.
findings.disposition: Existing qualitative obstruction; quantitative application only.

findings.claim: The complete c=-q LCM rule has E>=3087/4096
findings.comparison: The exact LCM coefficient class was not stated in the reviewed earlier record, but NS74 already displays the same exterior-aware Mellin evaluator and the same floor function F_beta=(2*beta-1)*(1-beta)^2/beta^6. NS96 uses a sign inequality instead of NS74 inserted-zero annihilation; 3087/4096 is F_(4/7). Different hypotheses, same separating tool and constant formula. This is not a floor for the unrestricted optimum.
findings.disposition: Distinct application of an already recorded separator; no new fundamental wall, cofinal estimate or worldwide novelty claim.

findings.claim: Projected PSD LCM cone equals signed LCM span; nonzero pairing matrix indefinite
findings.comparison: NS95 already exhibits the ordinary-product pairing sign problem. NS96 proves a distinct exact LCM-space equality using elementary rank-one pairs and old-space projection. This is not a theorem that the actual signed gain is small.
findings.disposition: New scoped algebra in this record; underlying sign-loss issue already present.

findings.claim: A trace-normalized square is a fresh route
findings.comparison: With a free line-step scale, trace normalization does not restrict correction rays or optimized gain. Trace-one rank-one pairs retain both individual pairing signs. A bound on the total update after scale absorption is different.
findings.disposition: Remove trace normalization alone from proposed escapes; no general restriction theorem claimed.

findings.claim: Lower-bound the actual joint signed observations
findings.comparison: This is the pre-existing open cofinal input. NS83 excludes a fixed error fraction at every doubling, not a compatible a/j lower gain or every compatible fixed gain per squaring. NS74 and NS95 arbitrary-residual countermodels do not refute an estimate for the actual target.
findings.disposition: Still open; not a new direction or a proved wall.
